title: Meta fined $25 billion over user deception

slides.headline: Meta fined $25 billion over user deception
slides.subtitle: A New Mexico judge issued the massive penalty.

slides.explanation: To put that in perspective, this fine is larger than the annual GDP of several small countries. It is a staggering amount for a single legal judgment.

slides.headline: Meta calls the massive fine a tax on speech
slides.explanation: The company argues the penalty is legally unjust. This follows an earlier $18 billion settlement Meta reached with 48 other states regarding similar claims.
Four independent news outlets including France 24 and TechCrunch verified the ruling. The consensus across these sources confirms the scale of the fine.

slides.subtitle: Read the full story on Headlinne.

caption:
A New Mexico judge has ordered Meta to pay $25 billion following a jury decision that found the company deceived users

during the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

The ruling marks a significant legal escalation for the tech giant.

This penalty comes shortly after Meta settled similar claims with 48 other states for $18 billion. Meta has publicly pushed back, characterizing the new fine as a tax on speech rather than a fair judgment.

We are tracking how this precedent might impact future tech regulations. Does this ruling change how you view data privacy policies?

story.title: Meta fined $25 billion in New Mexico over Cambridge Analytica scandal
story.summary: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company deceived users in a case linked to the Cambridge Analytica scandal, media reported Wednesday. The ruling follows an $18 billion settlement with 48 other states over similar claims. Meta called the penalty “a tax on speech.”
